content.text:
No findings.

I reviewed `origin/main...HEAD` and traced the model flow from hook parsing through session state to committed checkpoint metadata. The functional change is consistent: `Model` is now propagated on the added lifecycle events for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Vogon, and [cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/checkpoint.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/checkpoint.go#L376) now guarantees `"model"` is serialized in `metadata.json` even when empty. I did not find a regression in existing consumers; unmarshalling older checkpoints without the field still leaves `Model` as `""`, which matches the new contract.

Residual risk is limited to coverage rather than behavior: I did not see a test that asserts the serialized `metadata.json` contains `"model": ""` when the model is unknown, so the “always present” schema guarantee is not directly pinned by tests yet.

Verified with:
```bash
go test ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/cursor ./cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint ./e2e/testutil
```
I’m adding a checkpoint serialization test that checks the on-disk `metadata.json` includes `"model": ""` when no model is known, since that’s the contract this branch introduces.

I found existing checkpoint serialization tests in [cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/checkpoint_test.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/checkpoint_test.go). I’m placing the new case alongside the other field-presence tests and asserting both the parsed value and the raw JSON key presence.

I’m editing the checkpoint tests now. The new test will write a committed checkpoint without a model, then inspect the session-level `metadata.json` to confirm the parsed value is empty and the raw JSON still contains the `"model"` key.
The test is in place. I’m running the checkpoint package tests to verify the assertion and catch any formatting or lint issues in that file.
